text:
claire: quick note 1 proposing a minimal handling mode for transient/unscoped API keys so we can flip on strict project scoping without mass breakage.

nina: curious for specificswhat endpoints remain allowed?

claire: allow read-only inference (generate/embeddings), health, and metadata read. deny any state-changing or billing endpoints.

aditya: + enforce header requirements for any attempt to claim a project: `X-Redwood-Project` + short-lived `Delegation-Proof`. without both -> 403.

sam: billing concern: assign unscoped traffic to a placeholder billing tenant per-region so costs are visible. finance can reconcile later.

claire: rollout idea: observe (metrics + owner hints) -> restricted (rate-limits + deny-list) -> enforced (reject non-public). 60/30/90-ish windows.

aditya: telemetry: tag calls with `api_key.scope=unscoped`; sample allowed calls at 0.5% but log all denies/quarantines. alert if top unscoped keys > 5% traffic.

ops-bot: [deploy-bot] staged dry-run complete; backstop routing increased batching CPU ~2.5x under synthetic burst.

sam: mitigation: throttle and auto-quarantine high-volume unscoped keys; require verified account for new unscoped key creation.

nina: UX: console to show unscoped keys list + one-click claim & rotate flow. SDK should warn when env key is unscoped.

claire: service boundary rule: internal services must reject unscoped keys entirely. use mTLS/JWT for S2S.

aditya: volunteers? I'll write initial RFC draft. sam own abuse/alerts, nina own console UX, ops run canary.

claire: thanks all. landing doc next week.
